text: I think it's a poor proxy in most cases, but the legislators knew they needed a proxy, and income is the most objective measure. If it were based on what the child needs, you would have to define needs in a very narrow way. Some children need a lot more money. Some need a lot less. Would you require that children take an equivalent course at school? That they go to the same level of doctor? What if a child has medical conditions? That's quite difficult to define. So what they've done is to say that if you're in the middle income bracket, you're likely to need this amount of money for a child, and we'll just take that as the benchmark. And then you can vary it up and down. And then the courts have some discretion to vary it up or down, but they have to justify why. So it's a rough guide, but it's a workable one, and it gets you around a lot of fights, a lot of fights about what the child needs.
